targetItems.lockedItemText: Mathematical tractability supports theism only comparatively: the relevant question is whether rationally ordered nature and truth-responsive minds are more expected under purposive rational grounding than under specified naturalistic alternatives.

Personal and moral experience contributes modestly when it converges with public considerations and is tested against psychological, cultural, and competing religious explanations rather than treated as self-authenticating.

The considerations should be treated as partially dependent evidence whose combined force is discounted wherever one item presupposes another, preventing interpretive accommodation from being counted again as independent support.

referencedMoves.proposition: The effectiveness of mathematics in describing the physical universe is expected if a divine mind grounds both cosmic rationality and human rational capacities, but is surprising under naturalism.

referencedMoves.proposition: Christian commitment rests on cumulative evidence comprising resurrection testimony, intellectual inference, personally testable promises of Christ, and observed transformation in lived experience.
referencedMoves.sourceExcerpt: there are many things in science as we know that are not testable you can't test the origin of life in the lab you have to make an inference to the best explanation and the past and that is true of many things so for me the evidence on which my faith is based is cumulative part of it is objective intellectual arguments and all this kind of thing but a great deal of it has to do
referencedMoves.evidenceBasis: Lennox invokes inference to the best explanation for past events and describes objective intellectual, resurrection, experiential, and transformational components of his faith.
